2	 * Lakeview Labs & Kidney Care: FOLIO export, version 1.
3	 *
4	 * Lakeview runs an outreach reference laboratory and a nephrology clinic on one system. The export is a
5	 * row-for-row copy of that system's tables. Every payload entry is one table row; its `type` is the table
6	 * name. Column names are the database's own (UPPER_SNAKE). Codes are Lakeview's, documented below; the
7	 * tables at the end of this file list every code value in use.
8	 *
9	 * Two kinds of item, each with its own entry type:
10	 *
11	 * - **Lab report items** (`LabReportRow`): one item per requisition, i.e. one set of specimens drawn at
12	 *   one time for one ordering client. Holds exactly one LAB_REQ row, one LAB_ORDER row per ordered test,
13	 *   and the LAB_RESULT rows those orders produced. Published when every order on the requisition is
14	 *   resulted, cancelled or void (rarely earlier, with 'P' rows, when a slow test holds up a requisition
15	 *   with urgent results). Lab items have no author (system-generated) and no narrative.
16	 * - **Clinic contact items** (`ClinicRow`): one item per nephrology clinic contact (office visit or
17	 *   telephone contact). Holds exactly one CLINIC_VISIT row plus the VISIT_DX, VITAL, MED_ORDER and
18	 *   MED_STATUS_HIST rows entered during that contact. The narrative is the note the nephrologist typed
19	 *   and signed; it is short and is never generated from the rows.
20	 *
21	 * Changes: rows are never edited in place in the export. When a row changes after its item was
22	 * published (a result invalidated, an order marked entered in error), Lakeview publishes a new item that
23	 * `supersedes` the old one and restates every row of the requisition or contact with current values.
24	 * Exception: a medication's status changes are separate MED_STATUS_HIST rows in a later contact, not a
25	 * re-published MED_ORDER row. See MED_ORDER.MED_STATUS.
26	 *
27	 * Times: every timestamp column is RFC 3339 with the UTC offset in effect in America/Chicago at that
28	 * moment (e.g. `2026-02-09T08:14:00-06:00`). Date-only columns are local calendar dates.
29	 *
30	 * Identifiers: REQ_ID, ORDER_ID, RESULT_ID, ACCESSION, VISIT_ID, RX_ID and HIST_ID are Lakeview-assigned,
31	 * never reused, and unique across the whole export (not only within an item). Rows refer to rows in
32	 * other items by these ids.
33	 */

36	// Lab report items
37	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

39	/** One row in a lab report item. */
40	export type LabReportRow = LabReq | LabOrder | LabResult;
41	
42	/** The requisition: who ordered, when the specimens were drawn. Exactly one per lab report item. */
43	export interface LabReq {
44	  type: 'LAB_REQ';
45	
46	  /** Requisition id, e.g. "RQ-2602090412". */
47	  REQ_ID: string;
48	
49	  /**
50	   * Ordering client account code. Clients are practices that send work to Lakeview.
51	   * - 'NGFM': Northgate Family Medicine (outside primary care practice).
52	   * - 'LVNEPH': Lakeview's own nephrology clinic.
53	   * Other client codes exist for other patients; CLIENT_NAME always carries the display name.
54	   */
55	  CLIENT_CODE: string;
56	
57	  /** Display name of the ordering client, as on the requisition. */
58	  CLIENT_NAME: string;
59	
60	  /** NPI of the ordering clinician, 10 digits. Absent when the requisition was standing-order only. */
61	  ORDERING_NPI?: string;
62	
63	  /** Ordering clinician's name, "Last, First Credential", as typed on the requisition. */
64	  ORDERING_NAME?: string;
65	
66	  /**
67	   * When the specimens were drawn. This is the clinically meaningful time and the item's `effective`.
68	   * All specimens on one requisition share it.
69	   */
70	  COLLECTED_AT: string;
71	
72	  /** When the specimens were logged in at the laboratory. */
73	  RECEIVED_AT: string;
74	
75	  /**
76	   * Patient-reported fasting status at draw.
77	   * - 'Y': fasting at least 8 hours.
78	   * - 'N': not fasting.
79	   * - 'U': not asked or not recorded.
80	   */
81	  FASTING: 'Y' | 'N' | 'U';
82	}

87	 */

89	  type: 'LAB_ORDER';
90	
91	  /** Order id, e.g. "OR-7730412". */
92	  ORDER_ID: string;
93	
94	  /** The LAB_REQ this order belongs to (always the LAB_REQ in the same item). */
95	  REQ_ID: string;
96	
97	  /**
98	   * What was ordered: a Lakeview test code (see `LabTestCode` at the end of this file). An order code
99	   * may produce several result rows: panel codes (e.g. 'LK-CBC') produce one row per component, and
100	   * 'LK-CREAT' also produces calculated eGFR rows.
101	   */
102	  ORDER_CODE: `${LabTestCode}`;
103	
104	  /** Display name of the ordered test as printed on the requisition. */
105	  ORDER_NAME: string;
106

110	   * (e.g. Northgate) keep this number as their link back to Lakeview.
111	   */
112	  ACCESSION: string;
113	
114	  /**
115	   * Specimen type.
116	   * - 'SER': serum.
117	   * - 'PLA': plasma (lithium heparin).
118	   * - 'WB': whole blood (EDTA).
119	   * - 'URN': random urine.
120	   */
121	  SPECIMEN_TYPE: 'SER' | 'PLA' | 'WB' | 'URN';
122	
123	  /**
124	   * Specimen condition noted on receipt or by the analyzer.

126	   * - 'HEM': hemolyzed. Potassium, AST and LDH can be falsely high. Results are still released, with a

128	   * - 'LIP': lipemic.
129	   * - 'ICT': icteric.
130	   * - 'QNS': quantity not sufficient; affected results have RESULT_STATUS 'X'.
131	   * - 'CLT': clotted.
132	   */
133	  SPECIMEN_COND: 'OK' | 'HEM' | 'LIP' | 'ICT' | 'QNS' | 'CLT';
134	
135	  /**
136	   * Where the order stands in the lab workflow. Integer code. This is a separate axis from each result
137	   * row's RESULT_STATUS: an order is 4 (resulted) as soon as its results have been released, and stays 4

140	   * - 1: ordered, not yet collected.
141	   * - 2: collected, in transit or awaiting testing.
142	   * - 3: in process (some results may be preliminary).
143	   * - 4: resulted (results released).
144	   * - 5: cancelled before testing (no results; see STATUS_REASON).
145	   * - 9: entered in error (wrong patient, duplicate order). The order is void. Any result rows it has
146	   *      were produced by the analyzer before the error was caught, still carry their own
147	   *      RESULT_STATUS (often 'F'), and must not be used.
148	   */
149	  ORDER_STATUS: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 9;
150	
151	  /** When ORDER_STATUS last changed. */
152	  STATUS_AT: string;
153	
154	  /** Free-text reason entered with status 5 or 9, e.g. "Duplicate order". Absent for other statuses. */
155	  STATUS_REASON?: string;
156	
157	  /**
158	   * Set when this order is a repeat draw of an earlier order (in an earlier requisition): that order's
159	   * ORDER_ID. Absent for ordinary orders.
160	   */
161	  REPEAT_OF_ORDER_ID?: string;
162	
163	  /**
164	   * Why the repeat draw was taken. Present exactly when REPEAT_OF_ORDER_ID is.
165	   * - 'HEM': the earlier specimen was hemolyzed. The earlier result is normally invalidated
166	   *   (RESULT_STATUS 'C', REPLACED_BY_RESULT_ID pointing here).
167	   * - 'CONF': confirmation of a critical or unexpected value. Both results stand; the earlier one is
168	   *   NOT invalidated.
169	   * - 'QNS': the earlier specimen was insufficient.
170	   */
171	  REPEAT_REASON?: 'HEM' | 'CONF' | 'QNS';
172	}

227	
228	  /** Reference interval as printed, e.g. "3.5-5.1", "<30", ">59". Text; may be absent for calculated tests. */
229	  REF_RANGE_TEXT?: string;
230	
231	  /**
232	   * Abnormal flag against the reference interval.
233	   * - 'N': within range.
234	   * - 'L' / 'H': below / above range.
235	   * - 'LL' / 'HH': critical low / high (phoned to the ordering clinician).

238	   */

1	/**
2	 * Consumer views, version 2: the small shapes a patient-facing chart app reads.
3	 *
4	 * These are defined by the consumer, not by any source. A mapper turns one source's FOLIO record items
5	 * for one patient into these rows. The consumer merges rows from several sources itself, so a mapper
6	 * reports only what its own source says, and never invents, infers from other sources, or "corrects"
7	 * what the source records.
8	 *
9	 * Contract (see `Transform`): the mapper receives every item one source published for one patient,
10	 * in no particular order and including items that were later superseded or retracted, plus an
11	 * `asOf` date. It returns the rows that describe that source's record as it stood at the end of that
12	 * date.
13	 *
14	 * Conventions for every view:
15	 *
16	 * - **Scope in time.** An item is in scope when its envelope `recorded` time is on or before the end of
17	 *   the `asOf` day in America/Chicago. Ignore items recorded later. Apply the FOLIO correction rules to
18	 *   the items in scope: an item listed in another in-scope item's `supersedes` or `retracts` (same
19	 *   issuer) is not current; supersession is transitive. Use only current items, except where a view
20	 *   below says otherwise.
21	 * - **Time zone.** The consumer displays everything in America/Chicago, the patients' home zone. "Local
22	 *   date" and "local time" below mean wall-clock date/time in America/Chicago (UTC-6 standard, UTC-5
23	 *   daylight time). A date-time with no offset and no zone (for example a phone's wall clock) is taken to
24	 *   be America/Chicago local time: report it as written, do not shift it, and do not leave it out.
25	 * - **Partial dates.** `PartialDate` strings keep the precision the source actually knows: "2016"
26	 *   means some time in 2016, never 2016-01-01. Never pad a year-only or month-only date.
27	 * - **Only what the source records.** Rows come from structured payload entries. Narrative text may be
28	 *   used to understand an entry but must not be the only basis for a row.
29	 * - **Evidence.** Every row lists the items (and payload entry ids) it was built from, so the consumer
30	 *   can show the source text behind a fact. Cite at least the item whose entry gives the row's current
31	 *   state.
32	 * - **Sensitive entries are reported, never dropped.** Report every entry the source holds, including
33	 *   ones it marks restricted, confidential or sensitive. Mark such rows with `sensitivity` (see
34	 *   `Sensitivity`). Whether a sensitive fact is shown or shared is decided later, by the patient, at
35	 *   disclosure time; it is never decided by a mapper.
36	 * - **Determinism.** Same input, same output: no clock, randomness, network or file access.
37	 */
38	
39	/** A FOLIO record item in its JSON form (see the FOLIO record-item spec). */
40	export interface FolioItem {
41	  folio: string;
42	  /** Item id (ULID), unique within the issuer. */
43	  id: string;
44	  /** did:web of the issuing organization. */
45	  issuer: string;
46	  /** Patient id at this issuer. */
47	  patient: string;
48	  /** When the clinical event happened: RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a full or partial date. */
49	  effective: string;
50	  effective_end?: string;
51	  /** When the issuer committed this item: RFC 3339 date-time with offset. */
52	  recorded: string;
53	  author?: { id?: string; name?: string; role?: string };
54	  /** The payload's schema: `type` names the entry type in the source's .d.ts. */
55	  schema?: { url: string; type: string; sha256: string };
56	  /** Ids of earlier items from the same issuer that this item replaces entirely. */
57	  supersedes?: string[];
58	  /** Ids of earlier items from the same issuer that were entered in error, withdrawn without replacement. */
59	  retracts?: string[];
60	  /** Markdown narrative with `<ref id="…">…</ref>` spans; "" if none. */
61	  narrative: string;
62	  /** Entry id -> entry, each entry typed by the source's schema; {} if none. */
63	  payload: Record<string, any>;
64	}

66	/** The mapper's entry point. `asOf` is a local date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. */

Judgment calls:

- **Which items count:** an item is used if its `recorded` time, converted to a Chicago date, is on or before `asOf`. Any item listed in another in-scope item's `supersedes` or `retracts` is dropped.
- **Labs:**
  - Results marked `C` (withdrawn) or `X` (not performed) are dropped, as are results whose order is void (9) or cancelled (5). `A` (amended) counts as final, `P` as preliminary.
  - The value comes from `VALUE_TEXT`, so ">90" becomes value 90 with comparator ">". The numeric column is ignored because 9999999 there is a placeholder, not a value.
  - Only tests the consumer tracks are reported, and only when the unit matches. Duplicate results are merged by result id.
- **eGFR:** the race-adjusted variant (LK-EGFR09A) is dropped. The equation is read from the result comment first and the test code second, because the old codes carry LOINC codes meant for a different equation (MDRD). The LOINC code is still passed through as the source gives it.
- **Medications:**
  - Current status is the latest status change for the prescription, or the original status if there is none. A prescription ever marked entered in error is removed entirely, and IV orders are left out as hospital-only.
  - "Status since" is the change date, the resume date, or otherwise the start date.
  - Stop reasons: ADR becomes adverse reaction, PT becomes patient choice, and LAB, PROC and OTH become "other". The comment typed with the change becomes the reason text.
  - The source's RxNorm codes are product-level, not ingredient-level, so the ingredient RxNorm field is never filled.
  - The ingredient name is parsed from the drug name, with a small brand-to-generic table; drugs with the same ingredient are merged, keeping the most recent prescription.
- **Problems:**
  - Diagnoses are grouped by their 3-character ICD-10 category so a re-staged condition (N18.2 to N18.31) stays one row. Z and T codes are kept separate. Each row shows the latest entry.
  - A condition whose latest entry is "ruled out" is dropped, and one that was only ever provisional is not reported.
  - CKD stage and albuminuria come from the latest visit-level assessment, falling back to the N18 code.
  - Onset dates appear only in the note text ("since 2015"), so I left them out.
- **Allergies** come only from diagnoses blamed on a drug: ICD-10 "adverse effect of" codes, or text saying "induced" or "associated". A drug class is narrowed to a specific drug when exactly one drug of that class appears in the same visit. The reaction is taken from the diagnosis ranked just before the adverse-effect code, unless that diagnosis is CKD, diabetes or hypertension. This is a guess that the samples can't test.
- **Vitals:** the time is the first blood-pressure reading, a second reading goes into the repeat fields, and phone contacts produce no row.
